latest_release.name: Kiri 0.2.2
latest_release.body:
## Security
This release fixes several security problems, most of them reported to us privately. Update now. Details are in the advisories on the repository's Security tab.
- **An image can no longer reach files on your Mac that you didn't share.** The Linux VM is now given `/Users`, `/Volumes` and `/private` (as Docker Desktop shares by default), not the whole disk, and mount settings that come from an image are checked more strictly.
- **A container's working directory always stays inside the container,** and so does the folder Kiri makes for it when it is missing.
- **A new volume is filled without following links inside it,** so a container sharing the volume can't send the copy somewhere else.
- **A malformed DNS query from a container can no longer stop the engine.**
- **Mac: containers can't reach other containers through the domain router** (`*.kiri.localhost`), and its "not found" page lists your running containers only when asked by one of your own machine's names.
- **Seccomp profiles are applied,** and the default filter matches Docker's.
- **Linux and WSL: containers are firewalled on kernels before 6.3,** and reach the internet there.
- **An `--init` container's first process keeps none of the engine's open files.**

## New
- **Compose has its own section** in the window.
- **Install with Homebrew:** `brew install --cask libracoder/kiri/kiri`.
- **Every menu in the window can be searched:** type to filter fonts and other long lists, with the arrow keys, Enter and Escape.
- **Windows: Settings → Import** brings images, volumes and containers over from Docker Desktop.
- **Loop devices work in containers** (`losetup`, disk images).
- **Container files in Finder show volumes and bind mounts.**

## Fixed and improved
- **Compose 5.7 and later attach again:** `docker compose up` and `docker compose logs -f` show output.
- **Testcontainers for .NET, MongoDB and LocalStack start:** Kiri closes a connection when the client asks it to, answers `exec` and `attach` as Docker does, joins a container only to its own network, and a file copied in straight after a start is there.
- **`docker exec` straight after a start finds the image's users,** and a start that fills a new volume no longer holds up every other container.
- **Saves made on the Mac reach file watchers in containers,** so hot reload works in bind-mounted folders.
- **`always` and `unless-stopped` containers come back after the VM crashes,** and Kiri restarts on the new version after every update.
- **A published TCP connection stays open however long it is quiet.**
- **Pulling several images at once can no longer damage the image list,** and a damaged one is repaired. A damaged container list no longer costs containers their logs, files or volumes.
- **A named pipe, or a program that never stops writing, no longer holds up the engine.**
- **Images with hard links to absolute symlinks unpack** (Supabase's PostgreSQL image).
- **k3d finds its nodes:** the name filter is a regular expression, as in Docker.
- **Images list newest first,** and a missing working directory is made for non-root and read-only containers.
- **A tmpfs volume keeps its owner and mode.**
- **Image update checkers (Watchtower, Arcane) work:** Kiri answers `GET /distribution/{name}/json`.
- **`docker inspect` reports a container's port bindings and exposed ports.**
- **Image names with encoded characters resolve** (`mongodb%2Fmongodb-atlas-local`).
- **`docker cp` never mounts a container's root twice,** and containers start and commit correctly on kernels with overlayfs index on (Arch, CachyOS).
- **Signals only reach running processes,** and a failed start leaves no DNS name behind.
- **Import brings volumes, containers that share a network and digest-pinned images across,** leaves a volume in use alone, and says plainly when OrbStack or Docker Desktop isn't running.
- **Windows: Docker works again after WSL restarts,** launching Kiri at login no longer undoes a Stop, and the window opens wha

macOS: setting to stop the engine when Kiri quits
Settings: show who owns /var/run/docker.sock, and let Kiri take it when it's free
Trust the system certificate store for registries (corporate root CA, UnknownIssuer)

detail.readme:
A tiny, fast container runtime for macOS, Windows and Linux.
Runs your Docker images and works with the docker CLI, Compose and buildx you already use.

Download · Features · Build from source · Releases

🇬🇧 🇮🇩 🇩🇪 🇪🇸 🇫🇷 🇮🇹 🇵🇱 🇧🇷 🇻🇳 🇹🇷 🇷🇺 🇸🇦 🇯🇵 🇰🇷 🇨🇳 🇹🇼
Kiri speaks 38 languages. Is yours one?

--- Kiri is a lightweight replacement for Docker Desktop and OrbStack, written in Rust. It runs containers in one small Linux VM (or straight on the kernel on Linux) and speaks the Docker Engine API, so your tools just work. The name comes from the Igbo word *ntakịrị*, "small". ## Why Kiri - **Fast**: a container starts and exits in about 2.5 ms through the Docker API. That's around 80 times faster than Docker Desktop. - **Light**: the VM sleeps after 60 s idle, the daemon stays at about 15 MB, and it wakes in about 0.15 s. - **Compatible**: `docker`, Compose, buildx, `docker login` and amd64 images through Rosetta. - **Local domains**: `http://.kiri.local`, with HTTPS from Kiri's own certificate authority. - **More than containers**: a one-command Kubernetes cluster and Linux machines. - **A native window** for containers, images, volumes and networks, plus a menu bar item. - **In your language**: 38 languages, on macOS, Windows and Linux alike. ### In your language Kiri's window and setup come in these languages. It follows your system's language, and you can change it in Settings → Appearance. In Arabic, Persian and Central Kurdish the whole window reads right to left. | | Language | | Language | | Language | | Language | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 🇬🇧 | English | 🇳🇴 | Norsk bokmål | 🇧🇬 | Български | 🇮🇳 | తెలుగు | | 🇮🇩 | Bahasa Indonesia | 🇵🇱 | Polski | 🇷🇺 | Русский | 🇹🇭 | ไทย | | 🇦🇩 | Català | 🇧🇷 | Português (Brasil) | 🇺🇦 | Українська | 🇱🇦 | ລາວ | | 🇨🇿 | Čeština | 🇷🇴 | Română | 🇰🇿 | Қазақша | 🇯🇵 | 日本語 | | 🇩🇪 | Deutsch | 🇦🇱 | Shqip | 🇸🇦 | العربية | 🇰🇷 | 한국어 | | 🇪🇸 | Español | 🇸🇮 | Slovenščina | 🇮🇷 | فارسی | 🇨🇳 | 简体中文 | | 🇫🇷 | Français | 🇫🇮 | Suomi | 🇮🇶 | کوردیی ناوەندی | 🇹🇼 | 繁體中文 | | 🇮🇹 | Italiano | 🇻🇳 | Tiếng Việt | 🇮🇳 | हिन्दी | 🇪🇹 | አማርኛ | | 🇱🇹 | Lietuvių | 🇹🇷 | Türkçe | 🇧🇩 | বাংলা | | | | 🇭🇺 | Magyar | 🇬🇷 | Ελληνικά | 🇮🇳 | தமிழ் | | | Missing yours? Translations live in [`crates/kiri/src/ui/lang`](crates/kiri/src/ui/lang); see [Contributing](#contributing). ## Install | Platform | Get it | |----------|--------| | macOS 14+ (Apple silicon or Intel) | `.dmg` from [runkiri.com/releases](https://runkiri.com/releases/), or `brew install --cask libracoder/kiri/kiri` | | Windows 10 and 11 (x86-64 or Arm, through WSL 2) | `.msi` from [runkiri.com/releases](https://runkiri.com/releases/) | | Linux (Ubuntu, Fedora and others) | `.deb` or `.rpm` from [runkiri.com/releases](https://runkiri.com/releases/) | The first time you open Kiri, it sets up a `kiri` Docker context. Kiri updates itself, and checks each new release's signature first. ## Quick start ```sh docker --context kiri run --rm alpine echo hello docker --context kiri compose up -d kiri k8s start # single-node Kubernetes as the `kiri` kubectl context kiri machine create dev --distro ubuntu && kiri machine shell dev kiri import # bring images, volumes and containers over from OrbStack or Docker Desktop ``` Docker's commands also work as `kiri` commands (`kiri run`, `kiri ps`, `kiri compose up`, and so on), and always target Kiri. ## Numbers `alpine` running `true` and removed, median of 30 runs, same `docker` CLI for all three: | | Docker Engine API | `docker` CLI | |----------------|------------------:|-------------:| | **Kiri** | **2.55 ms** | **14.2 ms** | | Docker Desktop | 213 ms | 243 ms | | OrbStack | 380 ms | 442 ms | Method and every other figure are in [`bench/results.json`](bench/results.json). Rerun with `kiri bench --network bridge --runs 30` while all three engines are running. ## How it works ``` docker CLI ─┐ compose ────┼─ Docker Engine API ─► kiri daemon ── vsock ──► guest agent (PID 1) buildx ─────┤ owns the VM clone3 → container kiri UI ────┘ ``` The VM uses a custom 10 MB kernel, and its PID 1 is a ~900 KB Rust agent. That agent starts containers with a single `clone3` into namespaces and a cgroup. There's no runc, no shim and no dockerd. More detail is in [docs/development.md](docs/development.md#architecture). ## Documentation - [Features](docs/features.md): everything supported today, release files and known issues - [Development](docs/development.md): building, running from source, architecture and repository layout - [Release notes](docs/releases) ## Roadmap Next are more ways to share (Tailscale and Cloudflare Tunnel, in 0.3.0) and Coolify support (0.4.0). See [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) for what's in each release. ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). To report a vulnerability privately, see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## License [Apache-2.0](LICENSE). Third-party licences are in [NOTICE](NOTICE). The guest kernel is Linux (GPL-2.0); its config, patches and the source offer are in [`guest/kernel`](guest/kernel). The name "Kiri" and the Kiri logo are not covered by the licence. Forks are welcome, under a different name and logo.
